speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are here for a rash on your scalp and forehead. Can you describe how the rash looks, including its color, texture, and whether there is any scaling, crusting, or fluid?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis (Cradle Cap). The presence of a red, scaly rash on the scalp and forehead in a 3-month-old infant, which can worsen with temperature changes, is characteristic of this condition. The family history of psoriasis is noted as a genetic predisposition but does not rule out the more common diagnosis of seborrheic dermatitis in infancy. No further testing is required at this time.
